paper_metadata.title: Mo and Ta addition in NbTiZr medium entropy alloy to overcome tensile yield strength-ductility trade-off

evidence.quote: In this study, single-phase NbTiZr and NbTiZr(MoTa) 0.1 medium-entropy alloys (MEAs) were investigated for their use in biomedical implants.

NbTiZr and NbTiZr(MoTa) 0.1 alloys were arc-melted followed by multiple processing steps of re-melting, cold-rolled at a reduction ratio of 40%, and homogenized at 10 0 0 °C for 4 h and furnace cooled.

NbTiZr and NbTiZr(MoTa) 0.1 alloys were arc-melted followed by multiple processing steps of re-melting, cold-rolled at a reduction ratio of 40%, and homogenized at 10 0 0 °C for 4 h and furnace cooled.
In order to make a precise comparison, the same set of conditions were used to evaluate commercial biomedical alloys like 316 L and CP-Ti.
A wear test was performed for the MEAs under investigation and two commercially available biomedical alloys, 316 L stainless steel and commercially pure Ti (grade-4), usually known as CP-Ti.

A transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of the 10% strained (via tension) NbTiZr(MoTa) 0.1 samples is shown in Fig. 6 (a). A completely homogenized matrix along with some wavy dislocations was observed in the elemental map (Fig. 6 (b)).

The lattice parameter of the equiatomic MEA measured from XRD decreased from 341 pm (NbTiZr) to 339 pm (NbTiZr(MoTa) 0.1 ) with the addition of Mo and Ta.
The lattice parameter of the equiatomic MEA measured from XRD decreased from 341 pm (NbTiZr) to 339 pm (NbTiZr(MoTa) 0.1 ) with the addition of Mo and Ta.
Alloying in ternary MEAs by Mo and Ta showed a signiﬁcant solid-solution strengthening effect, as seen in the P-h curves of the MEAs (Fig. 4 (a)).
Mo and Ta addition did eliminate the strain-softening effect and resulted in an increase of both strength and ductility by delocalizing the slips and due to multiplications of dislocations.
